# Write the title

Write `title` as a familiar noun phrase of 2–5 words naming the overall topic defined by the final `meaning`. Choose the name a reader would look for when browsing information about that topic.

Keep directly related activities, products, participants, resources and detailed conditions in `meaning`. Include one of them in the title only when it is needed to distinguish the topic's identity. The title names the topic; it does not restate everything admitted by its definition.

Choose the shortest clear wording that remains a faithful summary. Avoid inventories of the topic's contents and vague abstractions. Keep the established meaning unchanged while choosing the title. Check that the title contains 2–5 words.

# Synthetic example

The title names the overall topic of blue display panels. Its meaning states the component relationship; the title need not list text panels and indicator lights.

# Output
- `title`: a familiar topic name of 2–5 words summarizing `meaning`.
